name: Fire Law
reason: Source term 'Law of Fire' was reordered to 'Fire Law' for a snappier Western fantasy register, consistent with other elemental Laws in the show.
description: One of the elemental Laws of the universe, governing fire. Cultivators comprehend it in levels (Brody claims a third of it; the source counts ten levels), and masters like Zane can erupt with violet flames through its power. Weapons and treasures can be forged from combined Laws such as Earth Law and Fire Law, and only a rare few Supreme Lords have accepted the Heavenly Destiny of Fire Law.

name: Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms
reason: The source's 'seven Divine Kingdoms' was expanded into the proper-noun faction name 'Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms' to give the alliance a formal institutional identity.
description: An ancient alliance of seven divine kingdoms whose legends go back one hundred and sixty thousand years, to a massive war against the Dragon-blooded across the Chaotic Ocean of Stars. Three of its kingdoms were destroyed by the True Dragon's breath, leaving four surviving today. Across its history it has produced only six individuals powerful enough to found their own divine kingdoms, and Zane later travels there knowing no one.

name: Ray
issues: Family grouping pairs him with 'Ray Wood' (Ep 1310), which is an unrelated divine tree, not this character; do not merge.
reason: The Chinese prince Su Rui was localized to the short, regal-sounding US name 'Ray', fitting a royal addressed as 'Your Highness'.
description: A prince ('Your Highness') encountered around Eps 338-343 who wields elegant authority, silencing insults with a lifted hand. He promises to bring Isla to a banquet for Zane and shrewdly understands the insatiable hunger of ambitious fighters, courting Zane's allegiance. Corresponds to Su Rui, the prince who tempted Luo Zheng with Zhi Tribe beauties and his sister's freedom from Xiaoming Palace.

name: Ray Wood
issues: Shares the token 'Ray' with the character Ray (Eps 338-972) but is a completely different entity (a divine tree); must not be aliased to him.
reason: The source's 'Eastern Hibiscus' (Fusang, the mythical sun tree of the east) was localized as 'Ray Wood' to evoke the rays of the rising sun within the show's set of four Divine Woods.
description: One of the four legendary Divine Woods existing beyond the heavens: the Ray Wood in the east, the Sunrest Wood in the west, the Aetherwood in the south, and Janet's Lofty Wood in the north. Of the four, the Ray Wood has never been seen in the universe.

name: Supreme Lord Sword
reason: The source title 'Heavenly Venerate Bright Sword' was localized as 'Supreme Lord Sword', using the show's established 'Supreme Lord' rank in place of 'Heavenly Venerate'.
description: A legendary sword master and the master of Killing Sword Mountain, said to be a Supreme Lord capable of fighting a True God. He spent countless ages refining a single ultimate strike, and the white sword shadow Zane saw plunged into the mountain's peak as a young Adept belonged to him. The fact that his sword still stands suggests he is alive, and Zane studies his legacy for a workaround to reach that state.

name: Evil Jace
reason: The character's Chinese name Xie Lang (whose surname 'Xie' puns on 'evil') was localized to 'Jace' with the epithet 'Evil' preserving the source's wordplay and his menacing nature.
description: A rogue weaponsmith and early antagonist (Eps 18-25) who kidnaps Zane from under House Lowell's nose, carrying him off inside a tumbling forge to his mountain lair. Gaunt, cackling and predatory, he is the creator of the Hellfire Blade and intends to make Zane part of it. Corresponds to Xie Lang, the weapon refiner of Chongyang County who hides inside his copper furnace.

name: Aldrich
reason: The source's title-named Black Iron Demon King was given the proper US name 'Aldrich', a harsh, old-sounding name fitting a major demonic antagonist.
description: A major antagonist of Eps 132-145: the Netherlord, one of the Four Dreadlords. A massive-framed demon whose strength and speed amplify dramatically within his Hellfire, making him effectively invincible while it burns. Zane maims him with a trapped box that slices his arm to bloody chunks, and then devours his Hellfire with vortexes, stripping his advantage. Corresponds to the Black Iron Demon King, who was near-unbeatable while his Sacred Fire existed.

name: Zachary Anderson
reason: The character's Chinese name Zhao Zhao was fully localized to the US name 'Zachary Anderson', keeping the alliterative Z of the original given name.
description: A black-robed acolyte (Eps 223-226) who guards the Arcane Aurora trial and explains the crystal balls that identify each participant. His sword unleashes roaring, dragon-shaped energy (his source counterpart's blade is named 'Torch Dragon'), but he is left in stunned disbelief by Zane's effortless, silent mastery of the Aurora. Corresponds to Zhao Zhao, the black-robed disciple of the Big Dipper Sword Radiance Platform.

name: Passing the Torch
reason: The source's 'Torch Inheritance' (also 'Torch Flame Inheritance') ceremony was localized to the idiomatic English phrase 'Passing the Torch'.
description: A grand inheritance ceremony and trial (Eps 1059-1320) in which young prodigies compete, confirm their status and earn extraordinary rewards. Zane's incredible performance in Passing the Torch draws the attention of the most powerful Supreme Lords in the Alliance, who watch his every move. It corresponds to the Torch Flame Inheritance held by the Thirteen Palaces in the source.

name: Brianna Shaw
issues: Episode gender_signal is mixed (m8/f7) only because Zane's soul controls her body in this arc; the character herself is female, matching the source (Feng Nianyun, m8/f18).
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized to a US-origin name: 'Brianna' as a strong feminine name and the surname 'Shaw' for her family line; the Cobalt Dragon recognizes her by this full name.
description: A powerful woman of the Dragon Bloodline whose golden-eyed body Zane's soul comes to occupy after fusing with her Soul Core (Eps 901-954), while her own amused, sharp-tongued voice drifts into his thoughts from within. The Cobalt Dragon recognizes her name from his past. In her body Zane kills a Soul Sea Realm warrior, terrifying onlookers. Corresponds to Feng Nianyun, whose soul was sealed by the Great Soul-Sealing Technique while Luo Zheng controlled her physical body.

name: Capital
reason: The source's 'Imperial Capital' was shortened to 'The Capital' as the natural English name for the Empire's chief city.
description: The gleaming jewel of the Empire in the Eastern Territory, with towering spires and ancient power, home to the Sacred Vault, The Citadel and the great Houses. The Skyreach Sect takes up nearly a quarter of the city, several times the size of The Citadel itself. Zane sets his path there early in the story (Eps 11-267), and even figures who command absolute deference elsewhere in the Eastern Territory hold no sway within it.

name: Gauntlet
reason: The source's sect entrance trial 'Trial of Blood and Fire' was renamed 'The Gauntlet', a punchier Western term for a brutal elimination trial.
description: The Skyreach Sect's brutal selection trial (from Ep 38) that a thousand candidates enter after passing the Entrance Exam, alongside students from the Great Houses. Participants carry Student IDs that broadcast their location to the mentors' slabs while they survive layered Magic Circles full of Level One to Level Three Phantom Beasts. Afterward, peak masters select the best performers as apprentices. Corresponds to the Blue Cloud Sect's Trial of Blood and Fire.

name: Level
reason: Generic grading word ('Level Four Adept', 'Nature-Level', 'Level 3 Phantom Beasts'), not a standalone entity; the specific tiers it appears in are covered by their own entries.

name: Illusionary Arena
reason: The source's 'Illusory Space' projection dimension was localized as 'Illusionary Arena' to emphasize its use for sparring and trials; it is distinct from the larger 'Illusory Battlefield'.
description: A projection technology-like dimension (Eps 1033-1286) into which a fighter's consciousness or reflection is cast, letting combatants demonstrate their full strength without real injury. Illusionary Arenas exist across the universe, and strange simultaneous phenomena can ripple through every one of them at once. Zane loses a match there to Lavender's brother, and she explains that an Illusionary Arena is 'just a projection'.

name: Titan Strike
reason: The source technique 'Heavenly Demon God Fist' (also rendered 'Demonic God Fist') was renamed 'Titan Strike', swapping the demonic framing for titanic imagery to match renamed moves like 'Ogres Shaking the World'.
description: Zane's signature body-powered fist technique, learned from the single legendary scroll sealed in the Celestial Library (Eps 51+). Its movements include 'Ogres Shaking the World' and the more devastating second movement 'Ogre Horde', and cultivating it channels Life Energy to strengthen his Nether Essence. It is extremely demanding on the body, mirroring the source's Heavenly Demon God Fist whose first style is 'Demon Moves the World'.

name: Hellfire Blade
issues: Family grouping pairs it with 'Hellfire' (Eps 134-142), which is a separate demonic flame art used by Aldrich, not this weapon; do not merge.
reason: The source's 'Hellfire Sword' was kept nearly literal as 'Hellfire Blade'; the master sheet confirms it must not be called 'Flame Sword'.
description: Evil Jace's prized weapon (Eps 20-31), a blade he forged by letting it absorb fire for two hours during its Foundation Stage, and into which he intends to forge Zane himself. Eerie flames wrap around it during refinement before Zane's Mindscape devours its essence.

name: Hellfire
issues: Distinct from the weapon 'Hellfire Blade' (Eps 20-31) despite the shared token; the source renders this flame variously as 'Heavenly Demon Sacred Fire', 'Celestial Fey Sacred Fire' and 'Sky-daemon Sacred Fire'.
reason: The source's 'Heavenly Demon Sacred Fire' was renamed 'Hellfire' for a darker, more immediate Western register fitting a forbidden demonic art.
description: A black mist of demonic flame (Eps 134-142), an ancient and forbidden art known only to the most formidable demons of the Underworld. It devours one's very essence rather than merely burning, and within its influence the Netherlord Aldrich's strength and speed escalate to unfathomable levels, rendering him invincible until Zane's vortexes suck the Hellfire away at frightening speed.

name: Death Road
reason: The source's 'Road of Death' (a hidden trial, paired with the 'Road of Life') was localized with the word order flipped to 'Death Road', matching the show's 'Life Road'.
description: A hidden trial within the Cloud Road (Eps 380-459), one of two paths offered alongside the far safer Life Road. It contains separate dimensional spaces accessed via energy vortexes and is home to Nether Phantoms, Sky-Reavers, Karmafire and the Drake puppet; only the bravest disciples attempt it. Its intensity is far beyond what Zane, Finn and Lewis bargained for, turning Skyreach rivals into allies, and it may hold the real secret of the whole trial road.

name: Hailey
reason: The character's Chinese name Huan Ling was localized to the soft US name 'Hailey', fitting her quiet, understated demeanor.
description: A soft-spoken young woman in Zane's party during the Karma Hall / Illusory Battlefield arc (Eps 1273-1318), who wields a hook like her companions and stays quiet until she declares, softly, that she can take enemies out. She is nearly swallowed by a shadow before being hauled back by a teammate's hook. Corresponds to Huan Ling, daughter of the Holy Spear Faction's leader and the one member of the group who asks no questions.

name: Mysterious Luna Hall
reason: The source sect 'Mysterious Yin Mansion' was localized as 'Mysterious Luna Hall', replacing the yin concept with its lunar/feminine Western equivalent 'Luna'.
description: A deeply secretive fourth-grade sect of the Heartlands (Eps 433-717), aligned with neither the Righteous nor the Evil Factions and regarded as one of the region's oldest and most enigmatic Grade-Three Orders. Led by the legendary Elder Luna (~976 years old), it is known for a vicious, cruel fighting style and ruthless vengeance, having slaughtered the entire family of a well-known independent warrior who crossed it.

name: Mysterious Weapon
reason: The source's 'Xuan Weapon' (xuan = mysterious/profound) was localized literally as 'Mysterious Weapon', the canonical Tier 1 of the show's weapon hierarchy.
description: The lowest tier of the show's weapon classification: Mysterious Weapons, then Spirit Weapons, Mythic Weapons, Sacred Arms and Divine Arms. They come in low, middle and superior grades (a superior one costs about one hundred Crystal Cubes), and even a lower-grade Mysterious Weapon hums with a current of power to a novice like young Zane.

name: Mysterious
issues: Mostly lowercase-noun mentions of the weapon tier ('low-grade Mysterious weapon(s)', 'Mysterious-grade weapon'); the Ep 205 hit is an episode-title adjective fragment, not an entity.

name: Dragon-blooded
reason: The source's 'Dragon Bloodline Clan' was localized as the compact race name 'Dragon-blooded' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A web of races tied by dragon blood (Eps 434-898), with descendants scattered across the globe and receiving cities built to forge elite Dragon-blooded warriors ascending from the lower realms into weapons of unparalleled power. Zane trains for months in their grounds in Laws, soul tempering and cultivation. In the ancient war against the Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms they were all but wiped out, yet no one ever forgot the Dragon.

name: Violet Core Realm
reason: The source's 'Extreme Purple Realm' (also 'Purple Extreme Realm') was localized as 'Violet Core Realm', tying its name to the Violet-Core Physique of its champions.
description: A hidden world or dimension (Eps 709-1319), incomplete like the Upper World itself, which beams of light cannot penetrate. Its tailor-made training methods give its practitioners enormous physical advantages: one Inner-Core Realm woman ranks among the top three warriors in the Heartlands thanks to its power, and a First-Rank Violet-Core Physique holder is practically the face of the realm. Elder Apeiron travels frequently beyond it. Corresponds to the Extreme Purple Realm associated with Xi Youqin in the source.

name: Felix Sterling
issues: Master sheet calls him 'Sterling family leader' but Ep 58 establishes him as the third son of House Sterling; episodes are authoritative.
reason: The character's Chinese name was fully localized: the compound surname 'Zhuge' became the aristocratic House name 'Sterling', and 'Felix' was chosen as an ironically refined name for a cruel young noble.
description: An antagonist of Eps 58-118: the third son of House Sterling, a Soul Realm powerhouse with a reputation in The Capital and an explosive, unpredictable temper. After Zane knocks his brother Connor out of The Gauntlet, Felix orchestrates repeated attempts on Zane's life, first through his loyalist Miles and later by sending Graves and Roman Stryker to The Sunbelt. Corresponds to Zhuge Feng, the Third Young Master of Family Zhuge, whose brother Zhuge Hong was kicked out of the Trial of Blood by Luo Zheng.
